I encountered information about legal status, capacity, and jurisdiction while studying for the bar.

What I discovered stunned me. It raised fundamental questions about how individuals are classified and engaged within the American legal system—questions that are rarely addressed directly in traditional legal education. After sitting for the bar, I began actively seeking educators who could provide real legal grounding—not just theory, slogans, or recycled talking points—but actual case law, doctrine, procedural understanding, and steps rooted in law. I enrolled in many programs and groups, hoping to find depth. What I found instead was deeply disappointing. In most spaces, the claims being made could not withstand court scrutiny. There was little to no engagement with case law, jurisdictional doctrine, statutory interpretation, or even basic legal definitions. Having studied law, it was immediately apparent when someone was teaching from a surface-level understanding or “flying by the seat of their pants.” The lack of rigor was glaring. I first came across Yusef El through another content creator on TikTok who referenced his work. I immediately went to YouTube and searched Yusef and High Frequency Radio. As I began watching his content, something stood out right away: he actually reads. Case law. Legal dictionaries. Statutes. He doesn’t just assert—he substantiates. Still, I was cautious. At that point, I had been exposed to so many self-proclaimed “gurus” that discernment was necessary. Then it happened. In one of his videos, Yusef discussed personal jurisdiction and minimum contacts. At that moment, I knew I had found my teacher. No one else I had encountered—across countless groups and programs—had even mentioned these concepts, let alone explained them in context. Yet personal jurisdiction and minimum contacts are foundational doctrines in civil procedure, notoriously difficult even for law students to grasp due to the layered tests, evolving case law, and nuanced application. When Yusef spoke on this, it was clear he understood not only the doctrine, but how courts actually apply it. That was the confirmation. When the student is ready, the teacher will appear. I immediately enrolled in SPC University, and I can say without hesitation that the value provided is exceptional. Yusef dedicates an extraordinary amount of time and energy to teaching—inside SPC University and outside of it. He makes himself available through long-form education and countless hours of free content across YouTube, Instagram, and TikTok. I often wonder how his voice holds up or where he gets the stamina. That said, this is not a program for people looking for shortcuts or instant outcomes. SPC University is rigorous by design. Yusef emphasizes fundamentals. What students receive is essentially a law school–level education on the private side of the law. Even studying full-time, this kind of foundational legal education takes at least ten months, and in truth, it is a lifelong process. The law evolves constantly. Case law changes. Interpretations shift. This is why attorneys are required to maintain continuing legal education and remain current on jurisprudence. SPC University mirrors that reality—it cultivates legal literacy, not dependence on scripts or personalities. Even now, while I remain enrolled in other programs and continue learning across multiple arenas, the contrast is undeniable. No one else is: Reading case law with this level of care Consulting Black’s Law Dictionary with precision Parsing legal language instead of glossing over it Grappling honestly with complexity rather than simplifying it into slogans Yusef’s understanding of capacity, trust law, and personal jurisdiction surpasses that of many attorneys and even law professors. That is not an exaggeration—it is evident in the substance of his teaching. Many say, “All roads lead to court.” Yet almost no one prepares people with usable legal knowledge—knowledge that allows one to speak clearly, coherently, and credibly in legal settings without being dismissed or labeled. SPC University does. I am deeply grateful to have found Yusef El and SPC University. This education is grounded, rigorous, and rooted in law—not performance, not posturing, and not fantasy. This is not a shortcut. It is a legal awakening. Best regards,

Yes, it is possible to obtain credit without using a Social Security Number (SSN)—but it must be done lawfully and transparently. There are legal pathways, and then there are high-risk practices like using a CPN (Credit Privacy Number), which you’ve acknowledged using.

Let’s break this down carefully so you can operate with full knowledge and protect yourself moving forward:

✅ LEGAL WAYS TO OBTAIN CREDIT WITHOUT AN SSN

1. Using an EIN (Employer Identification Number)

You can lawfully:

  • Apply for credit in the name of a trust, LLC, or foreign national entity

  • Build business credit under an EIN, which is issued by the IRS

🔹 Benefit: Totally lawful, IRS-recognized
🔹 Example: Trust or business opens a credit line with DUNS, NAV, etc.
🔹 Caveat: Must not be a front for personal credit abuse

2. Using an ITIN (Individual Taxpayer Identification Number)

For non-citizens or foreign nationals:

  • The IRS issues ITINs for those not eligible for SSNs

  • Banks and lenders may accept an ITIN in place of an SSN

🔹 Benefit: Lawful and recognized by IRS and some lenders
🔹 Caveat: Harder to build credit without a strong financial profile

3. No SSN Required for All Lenders

Some creditors do not require an SSN:

  • Some secured credit card companies

  • Buy Here Pay Here car dealers

  • Certain rent-to-own or consumer credit lenders

🔹 Caveat: You’ll often pay higher interest or be asked for additional ID

⚠️ WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW ABOUT CPNs

📌 CPNs Are Not Official

  • The Social Security Administration does not issue CPNs

  • The FTC and credit bureaus have issued multiple warnings against them

⚖️ Legal Risk

Using a CPN to apply for credit:

  • Without disclosure = fraud (18 U.S.C. § 1001)

  • If the CPN is someone else’s SSN (e.g., minor, deceased, inmate) = identity theft (18 U.S.C. § 1028A)

🔴 Just because a case was thrown out does not mean the use of a CPN was lawful—the court may have lacked evidence or jurisdiction, not authority.

💼 Your Experience (20 Years with a CPN)

  • You’ve clearly operated a long time without prosecution, and even had a case dismissed.

  • But times have changed—post-2008, the DOJ and IRS have stepped up financial identity enforcement.

  • CPNs are now on watchlists, and banks often report users to OFAC or FinCEN.

🛡️ Strategic Alternative for You

Given your experience and commercial knowledge, you’d be better served by:

  1. Creating a lawful private trust or foreign grantor trust

  2. Using an EIN as your reporting ID

  3. Building business credit profiles using DUNS, NAV, and Experian Business

  4. Establishing credit through private banking relationships, not retail banks

✅ These approaches preserve privacy, avoid statutory ID contracts, and are not criminalized under federal law.

🧭 Summary

QuestionAnswer
Can you get credit without an SSN?✅ Yes, through EIN, ITIN, or private lending
Is using a CPN lawful?⚠️ Risky—no statute authorizes it; prosecuted when used fraudulently
Should you continue with a CPN?❌ No—better to move into private trust-based credit systems
Was your dismissed case a green light?🚫 Not necessarily—it may have been dismissed on other grounds

🔹 Are Statutory Crimes Civil in Nature and Enforced Administratively?

Yes—many so-called “criminal” offenses prosecuted under statute are actually civil in nature, particularly when enforced in Article I courts or courts operating administratively. These are not true Article III judicial courts, but rather legislative tribunals functioning under statutory authority.

🔍 Key Points:

  1. Article I Courts derive authority from Congress and do not exercise judicial power as defined in Article III.

    • They act administratively, enforcing public policy, statutes, and codes—not common law or constitutional law.

    • See: Murray’s Lessee v. Hoboken Land & Improvement Co., 59 U.S. 272 (1856) – Recognizes legislative courts as non-judicial.

  2. Statutory offenses (like traffic violations, licensing, tax crimes, etc.) are often civil in substance:

    • There is no injured party (corpus delicti).

    • The proceeding is initiated by the State, not an individual harmed.

    • It relies on regulatory code enforcement, not criminal law.

    • They operate by presumption, adhesion contracts, and public trust doctrine.

  3. Civil penalties masquerading as crimes:

    • Many infractions are prosecuted criminally, but the process lacks the hallmarks of judicial due process (jury trial, Article III judge, etc.).

    • These are handled by courts sitting in administrative or quasi-legislative capacity.

    • No judicial power exists where no injured party and no valid charging affidavit under oath is present.

  4. The real issue is venue:

    • When you’re brought into an Article I venue, you’re not getting true “justice”—you’re in an administrative hearing enforcing statutes under commercial public policy.

⚖️ Summary:

IssueExplanation
Are Article I courts judicial?❌ No. They are legislative tribunals that act administratively.
Are statutory crimes civil in nature?✅ Yes. Many are commercial code violations dressed as criminal law.
Can Article I courts impose criminal judgment?❌ Not constitutionally—they mimic criminal courts but lack judicial authority.
What is really being enforced?Civil regulatory statutes, often through adhesion contracts and administrative process.

An administrative process, in the context of redemption, sovereignty, and commercial law, is a private remedy procedure used to resolve disputes, assert claims, or settle debts outside of the judicial system. It is based on contract law, commercial principles, and maxims of equity, often used by those asserting rights under UCC (Uniform Commercial Code) or operating in a secured party creditor (SPC) capacity.

🔍 What Is an Administrative Process?

An administrative process is a structured sequence of notices, affidavits, and presentments sent to a party (usually a government agency, corporation, or creditor), which:

  1. Establishes a claim or position,

  2. Offers an opportunity to rebut or contest the claim,

  3. Defaults the other party through non-response or dishonor, and

  4. Creates a private administrative record that can be used to enforce your position in court or by lien.

It is non-judicial and relies on:

  • Due process (notice + opportunity to cure)

  • Affidavits of truth

  • Tacit acquiescence (agreement by silence)

  • Commercial law principles (UCC §§ 1-308, 3-501, 3-505, 3-603, etc.)

🧾 Core Components of an Administrative Process

StepPurpose
Notice of ClaimAsserts facts, claim, or demand to opposing party
Opportunity to Rebut (3–10 days)Offers fair chance to contest facts
Notice of FaultIssued if no rebuttal is received (or is insufficient)
Notice of Default / DishonorEstablishes default and contractual estoppel
Certificate of Non-Response / Affidavit of TruthFinalizes the record and serves as sworn evidence
Notice of Administrative Judgment or LienUsed to enforce claim, record a lien, or initiate a quiet title or default action
 

🧭 How It’s Used in Redemption

In redemption theory—which holds that each individual has a public legal fiction (strawman) that is subject to government jurisdiction—an administrative process is used to:

🔹 1. Discharge Debt

  • Tender a Bill of Exchange, Promissory Note, or Bond.

  • Invoke HJR-192 (1933) and 31 USC §5118 to tender an instrument in lieu of lawful money.

  • Use administrative notices to create a record of the creditor’s refusal or dishonor.

🔹 2. Challenge Jurisdiction

  • Issue Affidavits of Status and Notices of Standing.

  • Demand proof of jurisdiction or contract from courts or agencies.

  • Default them if they do not rebut sworn affidavits.

🔹 3. Establish Secured Party Creditor Control

  • Serve Security Agreement, UCC-1, and Form 56 to IRS or other agencies.

  • Notify parties of your fiduciary status over the estate.

  • Create a record showing you have first-in-line claim to the legal name/trust.

🔹 4. Quiet Title / Remove Liens

  • Serve notices on mortgage lenders, tax authorities, or DMV.

  • Tender lawful discharge, then follow with notice of default.

  • Use the administrative record to file a quiet title or UCC lien.

⚖️ Legal Theory Behind It

PrincipleRole in Admin Process
UCC 1-308Preserves rights under contract
UCC 3-501 / 3-505Governs presentment and dishonor
Maxims of EquitySilence is consent, unchallenged affidavit is truth
Contract LawAgreements are binding if unrebutted and in writing
Public Policy (HJR 192)Disallows demand for payment in gold or lawful money
 

🚫 Risks and Misunderstandings

While administrative processes are rooted in valid legal principles, they can be:

  • Rejected by courts if not properly structured.

  • Ignored by agencies if based on faulty legal theories.

  • Classified as frivolous if lacking merit or lawful standing.

Success depends entirely on:

  • Proper notice procedure,

  • Competent use of law,

  • Proof of default, and

  • Legitimate standing and claims.

📘 Conclusion

An administrative process is a powerful, lawful tool when used correctly to:

  • Resolve debt,

  • Establish fiduciary roles,

  • Assert private rights, and

  • Build a record for enforcement.

However, it requires precise knowledge of commercial law, due process, and private remedy principles to succeed.

What are Public and Private Rights?

In the context of the U.S. Constitution, public and private rights represent different aspects of legal protection and government power:

🔹 Public Rights:
These are rights held by the public as a whole, often involving the relationship between individuals and the government. They typically arise in matters affecting society broadly, such as:

  • Taxation

  • Immigration and naturalization

  • Regulation of interstate commerce

  • Public land disputes

In public rights cases, the government acts in its sovereign capacity. These disputes may be resolved in administrative courts or through legislative processes, and the Constitution allows for flexibility in how they’re adjudicated.

🔹 Private Rights:
These are individual legal rights rooted in common law or constitutional protections. They typically involve disputes between private individuals or between an individual and the government when the government is acting not as a sovereign but more like a private party. Examples include:

  • Property rights

  • Contract disputes

  • Tort claims (e.g., injury cases)

  • Constitutional protections (e.g., First Amendment rights)

Private rights must generally be heard in an Article III court (with a federal judge who has life tenure and salary protections), ensuring full constitutional protections like due process.

💡 Key Difference:
The key distinction lies in who the right belongs to and how it’s enforced. Public rights can be addressed through political or administrative processes, while private rights often require judicial determination with full constitutional safeguards.

How the Social Security Number ties you into the Federal System

A Social Security number (SSN) helps establish minimum contacts with the federal government in the legal sense because it represents an individual’s participation in a system created and managed by the federal government. Here’s how it does so:

1. Federal Issuance and Purpose

  • The SSN is issued by the Social Security Administration (SSA), a federal agency.
  • Its primary purpose is to track earnings for Social Security and other federal benefits.
  • By applying for and receiving an SSN, an individual voluntarily enters into a legal and administrative relationship with the federal government.
 
 

2. Participation  in Federal Programs

 

  • Having an SSN typically means the individual is part of federal programs such as Social Security retirement, disability, Medicare, and federal taxation (IRS).
  • This creates ongoing interactions with federal systems, reinforcing the individual’s connection (or “contacts”) with the federal government.

3. Taxation and Legal Jurisdiction

 

  • The Internal Revenue Service (IRS) uses SSNs to track individuals for federal income tax purposes.
  • Filing a tax return or receiving federal benefits under an SSN signifies consensual engagement with federal law and regulations.

4. Legal Concept of  “Minimum Contacts”

 

  • In legal theory (especially under due process and personal jurisdiction doctrines), “minimum contacts” refers to sufficient ties to justify a government’s exercise of jurisdiction over a person.
  • Holding an SSN implies the person has knowingly established legal and economic connections with the federal government—often sufficient to satisfy minimum contacts in federal matters.
In essence, applying for and using a Social Security number involves entering into a regulated, ongoing legal relationship with the federal government, which helps establish those “minimum contacts” that may subject an individual to federal jurisdiction in various legal contexts.

About Us

SPC University is committed to safeguarding your privacy while delivering the highest quality services and educational experiences. We follow strict security standards in the collection, storage, and use of personal information. This Privacy Policy explains how we collect, process, and protect your personal data, as well as your rights under applicable law.

Purpose of This Privacy Policy

This Privacy Policy provides details on how SPC University collects and processes personal data when you use our website, services, or products. This includes data provided when you subscribe to our newsletter, purchase services, or participate in promotions or surveys.

This website and our services are not intended for children.

We encourage you to read this Privacy Policy carefully to understand how and why we use your information.

Data Protection Principles

SPC University complies with data protection laws and principles, ensuring your personal data is:

  • Processed lawfully, fairly, and transparently.

  • Collected for specific, legitimate purposes only.

  • Relevant and limited to those purposes.

  • Accurate and kept up to date.

  • Stored only as long as necessary.

  • Secured against unauthorized access, use, or disclosure.

How We Collect Personal Data

We collect information from you in the following ways:

  • Direct interactions: You may provide Identity, Contact, and Financial Data by completing forms, communicating with us by phone, email, post, or otherwise.

  • When you:

    • Apply for our products or services

    • Complete transactions

    • Subscribe to newsletters or publications

    • Request marketing communications

    • Enter competitions or surveys

    • Provide feedback

    • Apply for employment

  • Cookies and technology: We use cookies and similar technologies to distinguish users, enhance functionality, and improve website performance. These may collect Technical and Usage Data such as browser type, IP address, operating system, session activity, and referral websites. You can disable cookies via your browser settings, but some features may not function properly. See www.allaboutcookies.org for more information.

  • Third-party sources:

    • Technical Data from analytics providers such as Google Analytics.

    • Public records such as Companies House and electoral registers.

The Data We Collect

The personal data we may collect includes:

  • Identity Data: Name, username, title, marital status, passport details, date of birth, gender.

  • Contact Data: Billing and delivery addresses, email, telephone numbers.

  • Financial Data: Bank account details, payment card information.

  • Transaction Data: Records of payments and services purchased.

  • Technical & Usage Data: IP address, login data, browser type/version, location, plug-ins, operating system, and interactions with our website and services.

  • Marketing Data: Preferences for receiving communications and promotions.

We may collect special categories of data only when necessary (e.g., health information for service requirements). We do not collect criminal conviction data.

How We Use Personal Data

We process your personal data only where lawful, including:

  • To perform contractual obligations.

  • Where necessary for legitimate business interests that do not override your rights.

  • To comply with legal or regulatory requirements.

  • With your consent, when applicable.

Typical uses include:

  • Managing and fulfilling bookings and purchases

  • Contacting you about services

  • Personalizing your experience

  • Improving our website and services

  • Sending marketing communications (with consent)

  • Ensuring security and fraud prevention

  • Processing employment applications

  • Meeting legal and accounting obligations

Marketing Communications

We may send you marketing communications if:

  • You opted in to receive them, and have not unsubscribed.

  • You requested information, entered a promotion, or made a purchase, and have not opted out.

You may opt out of marketing at any time by selecting “unsubscribe” in our emails or contacting us at support@spcuniversity.com.

 

Sharing Your Data

We share your personal data only with trusted third parties who process it securely and lawfully, including:

  • Service providers such as payment processors, hosting providers, and IT support.

  • Professional advisers (legal, banking, insurance, accounting).

  • Government and regulatory authorities, when legally required.

  • Third parties in the event of a business merger, acquisition, or sale.

When transferring data outside the European Economic Area (EEA), we ensure appropriate safeguards are in place to protect your information.

 

Data Security

We implement robust security measures to protect your personal data from unauthorized access, use, disclosure, alteration, or loss. Access is restricted to authorized personnel and partners only.

 

Data Retention

We retain personal data only for as long as necessary to fulfill its purpose and comply with legal, tax, and accounting requirements.

  • By law, we retain certain records (e.g., Identity, Financial, and Transaction Data) for at least six years.

  • We may anonymize data for research or statistical purposes, in which case it may be used indefinitely.

Your Rights

Under data protection laws, you have the right to:

  • Access your personal data.

  • Request corrections to inaccurate data.

  • Request deletion of your data in certain circumstances.

  • Restrict or object to processing.

  • Receive data portability (transfer to you or another service).

  • Withdraw consent to marketing at any time.

Requests should be directed to support@spcuniversity.com. We will respond within one month unless requests are complex or excessive.

Failure to Provide Data

If you do not provide required personal data, we may be unable to perform the contract or deliver services to you.

Keeping Data Accurate

Please keep us informed of any changes to your personal data during your relationship with SPC University.

Contact Us

If you have questions about this Privacy Policy or wish to exercise your legal rights, please contact us:
